title: Compliance Watchtower: policy-as-code sentinel for residency & retention drift
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Build a policy-as-code sentinel ("Watchtower") that continuously verifies data location and retention configuration across Redwood deployments and automatically surfaces or remediates deviations. The Watchtower should produce cryptographically verifiable evidence for audits, integrate with the Console alerting/rollouts, and support safe automated remediation paths for common drift classes (storage region misconfiguration, retention window mis-set, KMS key region mismatch, and missing audit logging).
acceptance_criteria: Policy registry with at least 6 canonical rules (storage-region, retention-period, kms-region, audit-logging-enabled, backup-retention, export-block) encoded in a single policy-as-code format and discoverable from the Console.
A sentinel service that scans control-plane config and runtime resources every 5 minutes and emits findings to the Console incident stream and to an S3 evidence bucket.

Automated remediation flow for low-risk findings (e.g., retention shorter than policy) that can be enabled per-customer with a manual approval fallback; remediation success rate > 95% in staging runs.
Evidence artifacts (signed JSON) for each finding containing before/after state and the responsible action id, retained for the configured audit retention period and exportable via Console.
Metrics & alerts: detection_latency_p50 < 5m, remediation_success_rate p95 >= 98%, false_positive_rate < 2% in the first 30 days of rollout.
E2E tests and a canary deployed to a dedicated test org that simulates drift and validates detection + remediation and evidence export.
Documentation for internal SRE and enterprise customers describing policy schema, remediation semantics, opt-in controls, and rollback procedures.
proposed_solution: Implement a lightweight Watchtower microservice that uses a Rego/OPA policy engine to evaluate canonical resource snapshots collected from control plane APIs (models: storage buckets, GPU cluster volumes, database replicas, KMS configs). The service will run as a clustered deployment in the control plane, use leader election for remediation actions, and write signed evidence JSON to a central S3-like store. Remediations will be implemented as idempotent operators (K8s-style) tied to a reconciliation queue; high-risk remediations require a two-step approval via Console (canary + confirm). Findings and remediation actions will be routed to existing Console incident flows and telemetry (Datadog + internal traces).

comments: 2026-02-21 - Ayesha Patel: Initial spike completed. Verified that OPA/Rego can express required constraints for retention windows and kms-region checks. Prototype rule set attached in design doc (see links).

2026-02-26 - Marco Chen: Confirmed leader-election approach using existing control-plane lease library. Plan to reuse existing reconciliation queue for safe idempotent remediations. Scheduling implementation tasks for next cycle.

2026-03-03 - Design Review (Lydia Grant): Requested that evidence artifacts include signed policy hash and the exact rule version to avoid ambiguity during audits. Also requested backwards-compatible schema versioning.

2026-03-05 - Security (R. Morales): Approved threat model pending KMS key rotation handling; asked to ensure watchtower does not embed secret material in evidence blobs and that signatures use a dedicated signing key with restricted usage.

2026-03-09 - Marco Chen: Wireframes for Console incident integration pushed. Added a Console toggle to enable automatic remediation on a per-org basis. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/watchtower/pull/12

2026-03-10 - QA (Jin Park): Began writing e2e scenarios that simulate drift types: bucket-region drift, retention-truncated, and kms-mismatch. Found one false-positive around transient replication delays; added a 2-minute grace window to reduce noise.
notes: Goal is to minimize manual audit toil for enterprise customers and provide deterministic remediation paths.
Aim to make the policy registry pluggable so product teams can extend rules for vertical-specific controls without shipping new code.
Consider future integration with Dedicated tenancy controls to surface drift across reserved capacity nodes.
